For the MBA, INSEAD states it has 'doubled our scholarship funds' over three years and offers 'over 170 scholarship funds' across Fontainebleau and Singapore in need-based, merit-based and spot varieties. For the Master in Finance, Diversity, Excellence and Future Finance Leaders Women's Scholarship awards are made in each admission round with no application required.

No English test is required if English is your native language or you hold a university degree taught exclusively in English; in all other cases an English test result is required, with recommended tests and scores set out in INSEAD's language policy. applicant_utility.summary: INSEAD's own awards are tuition discounts, not full rides: the average MIM scholarship is €14,500 against €57,870 of tuition, the average MBA award is €24,000 against €109,860, and the average MIF award is €10,000 against €57,870. You cannot be considered before you start the programme application, and the two routes differ - MIM Diversity/Achievement and all MIF awards are automatic with admission, while named MIM awards need a dedicated form and only exist in Rounds 1-3 (or 1-2 for L'Oréal for Youth). Because 38% of participants receive funding, plan to self-finance the majority of the fee plus all living costs in France or Singapore, and treat any award as a bonus that arrives only after the admission decision.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates and early-career professionals who can fund most of a €57,870-€109,860 programme themselves and want a partial tuition discount - especially women, candidates who add nationality or sector diversity, and applicants who can document genuine financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Book the GMAT or GRE early - it is mandatory for every candidate and scores feed the same review as the scholarship
Apply in the earliest round you can be fully ready for: for the August 2027 intake, MIM Round 1 closed 06 October 2026 and Round 2 closes 08 December 2026, while MBA Round 2 closes 03 November 2026
If you want a named MIM award, confirm the round you will be admitted in is inside its window before you rely on it (Kung Family and Qinqin & Xin Zhang: Rounds 1-3; L'Oréal for Youth: Rounds 1-2)

MBA candidates: after submitting, open the scholarship portal and pick up to 4 scholarships before that round's cut-off - the August 2027 Round 1 scholarship deadline is 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CET and late applications are refused
Prepare exact financial figures for the need-based review, since INSEAD asks for 'accurate details of your financial situation'

Line up recommenders, an official transcript and CV now, and only skip an English test if you are a native speaker or your whole degree was taught in English - residency in an English-speaking country does not count
common_rejection_risks: Assuming an award is guaranteed: 62% of MIM participants receive no scholarship at all, so a funding plan built on an award is a funding plan with a hole in it
Missing a named MIM scholarship because you were admitted in Round 4, after that award's round window had closed
Missing the MBA scholarship portal deadline because it runs on its own calendar, separate from the admissions round
Submitting incomplete financial details, which undermines the need-based review
Non-European candidates leaving the visa file too late - INSEAD warns the process can take months and cannot start more than six months before departure
Expecting the award to cover living costs or flights, which these tuition scholarships do not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: After an average award you still self-fund roughly €43,370 of MIM tuition (€57,870 minus €14,500), €85,860 of MBA tuition (€109,860 minus €24,000) or €47,870 of MIF tuition (€57,870 minus €10,000), plus all living costs, housing, travel, installation and any optional items such as the MBA Business Foundations Programme (€2,040 in person / €1,530 online).
document_audit: Official transcripts and degree certificates must be uploaded as part of the application - start requesting them months ahead
Two letters of recommendation must be arranged in advance; late recommender submissions stall the file
English proof: a native-English background or a degree taught exclusively in English is the only exemption, and time spent living in an English-speaking country is explicitly rejected
MBA files need motivation essays, job-description questions and a campus choice on top of the standard set
The application fee must be paid for the file to be complete and reviewed
alerts: The MBA scholarship calendar is separate from and later than the MBA admissions calendar, but it is still a hard cut-off with no late submissions accepted
Named MIM awards are round-bound, so a late application round can silently disqualify you from them even if you are admitted
No award email means no Diversity or Achievement scholarship - INSEAD states 'If you don't receive an email, you have not been selected for these two scholarships'
Some INSEAD funds cannot be combined: the published listing notes awards such as the Abu Dhabi Executive Fellowship 'cannot be cumulated with another INSEAD scholarship' and override a previous award
Scholarship decisions arrive roughly five to six weeks after each round deadline, so plan financing around that timing rather than around the admission decision alone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online programme application with GMAT/GRE, Kira video interview, documents and fee inside an admission round; MIM Diversity/Achievement and MIF Diversity/Excellence/Future Finance Leaders decisions then ride on the admission outcome, while named MIM awards and MBA scholarship-portal selections are assessed on their own round calendar and notified by email.

applicant_utility.summary: ENS de Lyon's scholarships of excellence are €1,000-per-month living stipends - 12 months for the Ampère scholarship, 10 months for GRADUATE + - decided with your Master's admission rather than through a separate competition, because one online form covers both. The 2026-2027 round closed on 23 January 2026, so the realistic next window opens in November 2026 for 2027-2028 entry, with results around mid-March. The stipend does not touch tuition: international Master's students outside the EU/EEA and comparable categories paid €3,950 in registration fees for 2026-2027 on top of housing, the CVEC contribution and everyday living costs in Lyon.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-European students holding a degree obtained abroad who are entering an ENS de Lyon or Lyon/Saint-Etienne graduate-initiative Master's in exact sciences, arts or humanities and social sciences, can cover tuition and housing themselves, and need a monthly stipend to live in Lyon.
application_readiness_checklist: Choose your target programme from the right list first: Ampère excludes FEADéP and a few Master's programmes, while GRADUATE + only covers the CORE, DynLifeSys, MathInfi and PACE initiatives, with PACE open to M2 applicants only
Identify your profile before the form opens - European, non-European with a foreign degree, or non-European with a French degree - because the wrong form is an automatic rejection
Arrange officially certified French or English translations of every diploma and transcript, since documents in other languages are not accepted

Draft the motivation letter and CV in French or English and assemble programme-specific extras such as research projects or letters of recommendation; if one does not exist, prepare a PDF explanation instead

Check whether your chosen programme requires English or French certificates and book only a test that appears in ENS de Lyon's grids, unless you studied in a French- or English-speaking country or entirely in French or English
Upload everything in one complete pass well before the late-January deadline, as the office will not pre-validate your file
common_rejection_risks: Submitting on the wrong form for your profile, which ENS de Lyon states will not be considered
Uploading an incomplete file - the International Student Office explicitly does not pre-validate applications, so a missing item ends the review
Emailing the application instead of using the online form
Applying after the late-January cut-off, in a call that runs only once a year
Providing diplomas or transcripts in a language other than French or English without an officially certified translation
Applying to a GRADUATE + PACE programme at M1 level or to a non-listed programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the €1,000 monthly stipend, budget for registration fees (€3,950 for 2026-2027 international Master's students outside the EU/EEA and comparable categories; €255 for students in the listed French, EU/EEA, Monaco, Andorra, Quebec, Swiss, long-term-resident, refugee and subsidiary-protection categories), the CVEC student-life contribution, housing in Lyon, health insurance and travel to France. For US-enrolled students the separate Lafayette Fellowship adds a €1,500 monthly stipend for 12 months plus tuition coverage and round-trip airfare, but it must be applied for on its own.
document_audit: Official identity document, not a copy of a passport photo page alone - 'official' is specified
Translations must be officially certified; a self-made translation is not accepted
Current-year proof of enrollment is required in addition to past diplomas
Programme-specific extras vary by Master's - check the programme description before assuming the standard set is enough
If a requested document genuinely does not exist, the file needs a written PDF explanation rather than a blank upload
alerts: The call is annual and single-round: it opened 14 November 2025 and closed 23 January 2026 at 11:59pm CET last cycle, with the 2027-2028 calendar only published in November 2026
Decisions are not given by phone, and admitted candidates receive a letter of pre-enrolment rather than an instant confirmation
GRADUATE + money comes from the French government's SFRI programme, so award continuity can depend on that national funding framework

US, Canadian and Indian students enrolled in their own country can stack a second, separate scheme (Lafayette Fellowship, or an Embassy of France scholarship) - but each has its own application and deadline
Language certificates are only accepted from ENS de Lyon's reference grids, so an exotic or outdated test score may be rejected even if it looks strong
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the single online form matching your profile, upload the complete document set, and submit before the late-January cut-off; the admission committee reviews the Master's application and the scholarship together, and admitted candidates are informed by a letter of pre-enrolment, with results published around mid-March.
